The data infrastructure supporting clinical quality registries in Denmark is actively expanding to integrate primary care records. A central component of this effort involves the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark), which operates within the broader framework of the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme). 

To ensure comprehensive monitoring of patient pathways, the registry's data pipeline is being upgraded to ingest information directly from general practitioners. Currently, data has begun flowing in from general practice into a test version of the infrastructure [^src1]. This transition toward incorporating primary care inputs represents a critical evolution in the region's clinical quality tracking capabilities, bridging the gap between hospital-based treatments and general practice follow-ups. Because the available evidence for this specific infrastructure update is limited to this initial testing phase, further details on the full rollout timeline or technical architecture are not yet documented in the corpus.
